newsitem.title: USA: Nellcor to buy Aequitron in stock swap.
newsitem.headline: Nellcor to buy Aequitron in stock swap.

text.p: Nellcor Puritan Bennett Inc and Aequitron Medical Inc said Tuesday their boards had approved a definitive agreement under which Nellcor will acquire Aequitron in a stock swap worth about $61 million.
Under the agreement, shareholders of Minneapolis-based Aequitron will receive 0.432 share of Nellcor for each outstanding share of Aequitron.
This is equivalent to $10.75 per Aequitron share, based on the September 9 closing price of Nellcor, the companies said.
The exchange ratio is subject to adjustment based on the trading value of Nellcor shares for the 10-day period ending on the fifth trading day prior to a special meeting of Aequitron shareholders.
The ratio is fixed within a range between $23.14 and $26.61 a share for Nellcor, and a maximum of 0.440 share of Nellcor for each Aequitron share.
The acquisition is intended to qualify as a tax-free reorganization and a pooling-of-interests for tax and financial reporting purposes.

Aequitron makes electronic respiratory products for home health care and hospital use, and wheelchair lifts and automobile hand controls. For the fiscal year ended April 30, 1996, it reported revenues of $38.5 million.

"The acquisition of Aequitron is another excellent strategic fit for Nellcor Puritan Bennett," C. Raymond Larkin Jr., Nellcor president, said in a statement. "Aequitron's product line is complementary to our own and includes a line of compact, portable ventilators which fills an important gap in our ventilator product line."
After the acquisition, Nellcor will have the broadest ventilator line in the industry, he added.
The acquisition is subject to several conditions, including approval by regulators and stockholders of Aequitron.
